This relationship is inferred through a chain of interactions: the compound is identified as a target of Firategrast, which in turn targets the disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 9. The final score of 0.5885 indicates a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that the compound may modulate the activity of this protein. The mechanism involves the compound acting as a ligand for Firategrast, which then inhibits the disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 9. The evidence supports a possible regulatory role of the compound in the function of this protein, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction.
